subject: Hosting & region gateways — follow-up on residency and routing constraints
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Lena Novak <lena@novabank.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2025 16:12:00 +00:00
Subject: Hosting & region gateways — follow-up on residency and routing constraints

Hi Lena — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single place to track constraints and decisions.

Key takeaways from today: 
- NovaBank requires production customer data to remain physically in the EU (no cross-border movement to non-EU regions) for regulated payment flows.
- Non-production (dev/staging) can reside in the US for now, but security wants clear separation and an audit trail when data is promoted.
- APAC usage is an upcoming requirement (Q4) but initially lower priority — may require separate region availability.

Immediate questions for you (so we can align hosting modes):
1) Confirmed: is EU-only residency a strict requirement for all production datasets, or only for card/transaction-related payloads?
2) Do you have a preference for Private VPC/on-prem when residency is strict, or would Dedicated (single-tenant capacity located in EU) be acceptable if we can guarantee data never leaves the region?
3) Any minimum SLA or throughput targets we should presume for the pilot (RPS / tokens per minute)?

What we propose next: 
- Technical proposal: pilot on Dedicated capacity in the Frankfurt region (eu-central-1) for production-sensitive flows + Private VPC for administrative/credential management. Hosted API could be used for lower-sensitivity, user-facing features to accelerate time-to-value.
- Security pack: attached a condensed SOC2 summary and an EU-hosting matrix for how we map model variants and KV caching rules by region.
- Procurement: please share the completed questionnaire (I’ve attached a blank copy) and your procurement contact; we’ll prepare a draft SOW and estimate.

Attachments: redwood-eu-hosting-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (pdf), NovaBank_procurement_questionnaire.xlsx (blank)

Next steps / owners: 
- Lena: confirm Q1 & Q2 above and provide procurement contact (Anna or a PG?) — target by EOD Wed.
- Jordan: follow up with a rough cost/latency estimate for Dedicated vs Private VPC (end of week).
- Ben: validate feasibility of KV cache and token routing restrictions for EU-only flows (internal tech check).

Thanks — I'll schedule a short follow-up once we have the answers.

—
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0193
From: Lena Novak <lena@novabank.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Anna Ross <anna.ross@novabank.com>, procurement@novabank.com, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2025 18:05:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Hosting & region gateways — follow-up on residency and routing constraints

Thanks Jordan — useful summary. Quick clarifications: 
- EU residency applies to all production PII and payment transaction payloads. We can tolerate non-EU processing for aggregated analytics and anonymized telemetry, but not for transaction/PII.
- Preferred path for production is Private VPC (customer-managed network) in an EU cloud region. If you can get the same contractual/data-flow guarantees with Dedicated (single-tenant) and provide auditable controls that demonstrate data never leaves the EU boundary, procurement/legal will consider it; however, Private VPC is currently the default ask.
- Pilot SLA: we don’t need island-level throughput for the pilot — aim for 200 RPS sustained and p95 latency < 350ms for inference requests. Production rollout will require higher targets; we can provide exact numbers after the pilot.
- APAC: we will open a separate discussion for APAC data residency — likely a second deployment later in the year.

I’ve CC'd Anna (legal) and procurement. Anna — can you confirm if a Dedicated contract with a data locality clause would be acceptable, or if Private VPC must be in the SOW? Procurement team — please find Jordan's questionnaire attached; we’ll fill and return by next Tue.

Regards,
Lena Novak
Head of Cloud Platforms — NovaBank

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2025 19:40:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Hosting & region gateways — follow-up on residency and routing constraints (internal)

Jordan / Marissa — copying my quick technical read and recommended path based on Lena's reply. Keep this internal until we finalize the SOW.

Summary of constraints: 
- Production PII/transactions must not leave the EU.
- Prefer Private VPC but Dedicated may be acceptable if we can (A) pin compute to eu-central-1, (B) enforce egress-blocking rules, (C) provide per-request routing proofs (traces that show host/region).

Recommended next steps (tech):
1) Pilot: Dedicated pool in eu-central-1 (fastest to spin up) with strict network ACLs and a read-only routing policy that prevents egress. Time to pilot: ~3 weeks to provision + 1 week to integrate KV cache and redis-backed session stores.
2) Production: If procurement/legal insist on Private VPC, plan for a Private VPC deployment (we have an on-prem/VPC packaging playbook). Time to production-ready: ~6–8 weeks (networking, KMS integration, audit logs).
3) Hosted API: keep it as an escape hatch for non-sensitive flows and for early-stage UX tests — no PII routing to Hosted in production.

Action items: 
- Ben: draft a short technical appendix that explains the egress-proofing and the telemetry we can provide (deliver by Thu).
- Jordan: include the appendix in the SOW and the cost delta between Dedicated vs Private VPC for a trial (deliver by Fri).
- Marissa: coordinate with Legal to understand contract language requirements for data locality.

I’ll start a lab spin-up for eu-central-1 tomorrow and document the provisioning steps in the shared Drive link.

—
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
